## [2026-10-15](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-15.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [CacheSmith: Accurate RAG Serving under Latency SLOs with Adaptive KV Reuse](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18925>)

CacheSmith adapts how much cross-chunk attention is recomputed when reusing cached RAG context, jointly choosing request batches and a warm-up, probe and patch plan under latency budgets. Its objective counts responses that meet both a generation-quality gate and a first-token deadline, helping serving systems allocate recomputation where it improves useful responses rather than latency alone.

**Published:** 2026-10-13 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T15:09:52.031Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** RAG, KV Reuse, Selective Recomputation, Latency SLO

**Public availability:** 2026-10-15T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AR/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18925>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Reviewed method, planner/scheduler Algorithm 1, runtime and all evaluation/ablation sections. vLLM 0.10.2 experiments use Llama 3.1-8B on one 96 GB RTX PRO 6000 and Qwen3-32B on two, EPYC 9554 and NVMe-cached chunks. Across 96 task/arrival/SLO combinations, authors exceed an oracle best-static configuration in 93 and report 2-27.5% higher quality-gated SLO attainment. Timing is inferred from CacheSmith's PRIMARY cs.AR Oct 15 batch plus official announcement schedule; Oct 13 is receipt, not asserted public release.

**Limitations:** Quality is estimated from offline demand profiles, not guaranteed for every request; experiments use four small benchmark-derived/synthetic tasks, Poisson/Gamma arrivals and precomputed SSD chunks. Majority signal selection can hurt minority requests in mixed batches. Query-context baselines share authors' untuned reimplementation because original kernels were unavailable. Quality gates are task-specific, not general answer correctness. No verified implementation release or independent reproduction; do not relabel the paper's 27.5% as percentage points.

## [2026-10-13](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-13.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Ember: Making Unified Virtual Memory Practical for Discrete-Memory GPUs](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13408>)

Ember keeps oversubscribed GPU allocations accessible in host memory and selectively promotes useful regions into GPU memory, with an adaptive variant using hardware access counters and proactive reclamation. This reduces page-migration thrashing when model weights exceed device capacity, offering a concrete memory-management design for constrained LLM inference rather than requiring the whole model to fit on the GPU.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:38:15.060Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Unified Memory, GPU Offloading, Memory Oversubscription

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.OS/recent>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13408>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery of the October 12 batch; October 9 v1 date retained, with public availability inferred from the dated listing and official schedule. Sections 4–8 distinguish stock-CUDA static placement from the patched-driver adaptive policy. Section 7.4 tests Qwen2.5-14B/Qwen3-32B generation on RTX 5080, A40 and H200, each capped to 16 GB; at 1.41x oversubscription, the static variant reports 4.7–13x over stock UVM.

**Limitations:** These are 128-token decode benchmarks, not serving throughput: no strategy exceeds 3 tokens/s in the oversubscribed cases. Adaptive placement requires a driver patch and administrator access; only managed allocations and one GPU-to-host tier are controlled. No dedicated source-code release was verified; the abstract's larger headline is not substituted for the narrower Section 7.4 result.

## [2026-10-13](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-13.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [SlackSwap: Bandwidth-Aware Activation Swapping and Recomputation for Memory-Efficient DNN Training](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13003>)

SlackSwap treats host-link time as a limited budget, offloading activations that would be expensive to rebuild and recomputing cheaper tensors once that transfer budget is exhausted. Its trace-driven simulations suggest that combining bandwidth-aware placement with asynchronous copies can retain training throughput under tight activation-memory budgets, while leaving real-system performance to be demonstrated.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:36:42.817Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Activation Memory, Offloading, Recomputation

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.DC/recent?skip=50&show=100>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13003>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery of the verified October 12 batch; original October 9 submission retained and availability inferred from the dated listing plus schedule. Algorithm 1 and Sections 3–4 specify two-pass planning, FIFO offloads and earliest-deadline-first prefetches. A100 simulations of BERT-Large, GPT-2 XL and a Llama-7B-style model retain 96.3–99.6% of unlimited-memory throughput at half the activation budget, 1.10–1.11x the best simulated baseline.

**Limitations:** All performance results are simulated. The model omits allocator fragmentation, copy-induced HBM contention, and shared PCIe/host-memory contention; model states remain resident on one GPU. The SwapAdvisor comparison omits its operator-order and memory-pool genetic search. No dedicated implementation or independent reproduction was verified.

## [2026-10-12](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-12.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13778>)

ReplaySSM represents recurrent state as a checkpoint plus recent inputs, avoiding most full-state writes and making speculative rollback a buffer operation. The new paper extends this approach with separate precisions for output reads and recurrent updates, reducing the feedback of state-quantization error during long generations.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:04:28Z · **Novelty:** material-update · **Tags:** SSM State, Speculative Decoding, Low Precision

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13778>) · [Blog](<https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/>) · [Code](<https://github.com/Johnny-Liou/ReplaySSM>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The new quantization study reports mean GPQA-Diamond losses of 13.05 percentage points for shared NVFP4+SR versus 2.36 for NVFP4 reads with FP16+SR recurrence across four hybrid models. Separately, FP32-state decoding at batch 256 improves whole-step latency by 1.20–1.47× on one H100 or B300 per model.

**Limitations:** Quantization accuracy uses emulation, standard decoding and full-precision prefill; residual errors remain. Performance gains shrink at batch 1. The public fork contains experimental paths beyond the upstream Mamba2 integration; benchmarks were not reproduced.

**Update:** 2026-10-12: the newly announced paper adds two-precision state algorithms and long-generation KL/accuracy experiments beyond the June 15 ReplaySSM blog (https://dao-lab.ai/blog/). The retained October 9 date is this arXiv paper's v1 submission date, not the method's first release. Paper-update availability is inferred as October 12 00:00 UTC from https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/new and https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html; the June method is not being presented as newly invented.

### [PageWeaver: KV-Guided Query Unions for Sparse Attention](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11201>)

PageWeaver groups sparse-attention queries by overlap in their selected KV pages, then executes them through a kernel that retains each query's original support and output location. This reduces repeated page traversal while accounting for the cost of constructing useful query groups.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-09T10:07:33Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Sparse Attention, KV Reuse, GPU Scheduling

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11201>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. On selected MiniMax-M3 H200 captures, online regrouping lowers complete-call latency by 3.26–7.66% versus original-order Union8, including preparation. Newly discovered: reviewed and deferred October 9; its inferred public release precedes this daily window.

**Limitations:** Incremental service throughput gains are only 0.47–0.73% at 32K/64K and negative at 8K. Few independent prompts, one generated token and no downstream quality evaluation; no win over the faster existing B300 backend. A dedicated public artifact URL was not verified.

## [2026-10-10](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-10.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [RaReCache: Bridging the Gap in Cross-Model KV Cache Reuse via Rank disagreement-based Selective Recomputation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11358>)

RaReCache maps an existing smaller model's KV cache into a larger model and ranks token positions using disagreement between full-rank and reduced-rank predictions. Recomputing only the selected positions lets the larger model recover part of the quality lost by cache mapping while avoiding a complete target-model prefill.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-09T10:07:33Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** KV Cache, Cross-Model Reuse, Selective Recomputation, Prefill

**Public availability:** 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11358>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Table 5 gives Qwen3-0.6B→14B GSM8K accuracy of 90.2 versus 95.1 target-only at 30% recomputation. Appendix B reports 1.95× GPU-busy-time speedup on A100 80GB, batch 1 and 2,048 tokens. Newly discovered: previously reviewed but deferred October 9; inferred public release is October 9 00:00 UTC, before this daily window.

**Limitations:** Already-completed source prefill is excluded; calibration is task-specific. At the same budget, MMLU-Redux retains only 77.9% of target accuracy. Low-load serving latency can worsen. Code release is promised after deanonymization/publication, not verified as available.

## [2026-10-06](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-06.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [MOLT: A Fine-Grained GPU Memory Sharing System for LLM Serving with Opportunistic Fine-Tuning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05748>)

MOLT lets inference reclaim individual saved activations from a colocated fine-tuning job, which recomputes them later instead of restarting its current training step. Tracking outstanding GPU work and coordinating reclamation across tensor-parallel ranks makes idle serving memory usable for adaptation while preserving priority for latency-sensitive requests.

**Published:** 2026-10-05 · **First seen:** 2026-10-06T10:03:46Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Memory Sharing, Activation Recomputation, Serving, LoRA

**Public availability:** 2026-10-06T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.DC/recent>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05748>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The October 6 announcement batch establishes eligibility; original v1 is October 5 03:53:21 UTC. Sections 4–5 and Table 2 evaluate rank-8 LoRA on Mistral-Small-24B and Llama-3.1-70B across four H100 SXM/B200 deployments. Under BurstGPT arrivals, MOLT completes 1.9–3.3x the tuning tokens/s of LLMStation+SIRIUS, with 99.7–100% inference SLO attainment.

**Limitations:** SLO means both TTFT and TPOT are within three times the inference-only mean, not unchanged latency. Evidence covers two models and trace-driven workloads, with offline activation/dispatch profiling and substantial vLLM/PyTorch changes; it does not establish adaptation-quality gains. No primary-linked public implementation was verified or experiment reproduced.

## [2026-10-04](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-04.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [MoE-CORE: Coordinated Expert Offloading and Residency for Memory-Constrained MoE Inference](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01950>)

MoE-CORE separates full-layer expert staging during prefill from routing-aware expert caching and prefetching during decoding on a memory-limited accelerator. Coordinating which experts remain resident with when missing weights move from host memory reduces decoding stalls for large mixture-of-experts models.

**Published:** 2026-10-01 · **First seen:** 2026-10-04T10:02:13Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** MoE Offloading, Expert Caching, NPU Inference

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01950>) · [Code](<https://github.com/LookAround0301/vllm-ascend/tree/moe_offload_v5.0/vllm_ascend/expert_offload>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Newly discovered from the October 2 arXiv DC announcement list. Original v1 was submitted October 1 at 16:11:45 UTC; the list and official schedule place public availability at October 2 00:00 UTC, inside the lookback. Under an 84-GB Ascend 950PR memory cap, batch-one DeepSeek-V4-Flash tests report 1.39–1.75x decoding speedups over load-on-demand across five workloads using matched 1K output caps and exact expert execution. Component ablations and source files are accessible.

**Limitations:** The separate vLLM Prefetch comparison uses a shorter 128-token cap and is not a matched-output end-to-end comparison. Tests use one NPU; initial-token latency can worsen, and expert residency is not jointly optimized with KV management. Optional expert substitution changes model computation without a demonstrated accuracy guarantee and is excluded from the cited exact-path result; no measurements were reproduced.

## [2026-10-03](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-03.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [RapidMoE: Exploiting Cross-Asymmetry via Adaptive Residual Offloading for Large-Scale MoE Inference](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01265>)

RapidMoE combines low-precision expert computation on GPUs with selectively higher-precision CPU work, using residual weight representations and importance-based routing to balance the devices. This reduces duplicated host-memory storage and offloading stalls when serving large mixture-of-experts models on memory-limited CPU–GPU systems.

**Published:** 2026-10-01 · **First seen:** 2026-10-02T15:33:57Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** MoE Offloading, Mixed Precision, CPU–GPU Scheduling

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01265>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Screened October 2 and fully reviewed for this catch-up selection: v1 is October 1 at 08:02:24 UTC; the October 2 announcement list and official schedule imply public release at October 2 00:00 UTC. A800/RTX 4090 tests cover DeepSeek-R1/V3 and Qwen3-235B; the authors report up to 3.5x decoding speedup over KTransformers, with accuracy checks, component ablations, and a 1,000-request serving workload.

**Limitations:** Serving tests use concurrency four and 0.2 requests/s; accuracy varies slightly against the Q4 reference. Calibration takes hours and performance depends on CPU memory bandwidth and hardware balance. These results do not establish high-concurrency cluster performance; no public RapidMoE implementation was verified.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [LMCache: An Efficient KV Cache Layer for Enterprise-Scale LLM Inference](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09665>)

LMCache makes KV caches reusable across requests and inference engines through a separate storage layer, optimized transfers, and a standardized connector. It lets serving systems trade GPU memory and repeated prefill computation for CPU or remote storage while also supporting prefill-decode disaggregation.

**Published:** 2025-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** KV Cache, Offloading, Distributed Storage

**Positioning:** open-reference

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09665>) · [Code](<https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The revised report evaluates CPU offload, remote storage, and disaggregated serving with multiple open models on H100 hardware, including real-trace-derived workloads and transfer-level ablations.

**Limitations:** Cache reuse depends on exact shared context and available bandwidth; remote retrieval can be slower than recomputation. Reported gains depend on the compared engine versions, and SGLang's native CPU offload performs similarly in one tested configuration.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19969>)

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash combines cross-layer cache reuse, sparse attention, FP4 KV storage, and approximate replay of sliding-window states to shrink long-context memory. Its encoder-decoder design also reduces prefill work, targeting the memory, storage, and bandwidth costs of input-heavy agents with up to one million context tokens.

**Published:** 2026-09-17 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** KV Cache, FP4, Long Context, Agent Workloads

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19969>) · [Project](<https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash>)

**Evidence:** technical-report; full-text. The report explains cache layout and replay mechanics and reports 890 bytes per token for global GPU-resident KV, roughly one quarter of DeepSeek-V4-Flash, with persistent cache around one eighth of that baseline.

**Limitations:** These are architecture-specific author measurements, not universal savings. Bounded replay reconstructs approximate states; the authors identify uncharacterized robustness risks at cache-resumption boundaries and in sparse long-context retrieval.
